name: deck-storyline evals
description: With/without skill comparison for storyline design tasks. Each case names an input prompt, expected signals the skill should produce, and bad signals the skill must NOT produce (typically visual-composition bleed, which belongs to a downstream skill). Every case also carries a `grading_rubric` (deterministic checks a subagent grader can apply) and a `gold_reference_spec` (an acceptable output shape, in YAML embedded as a JSON string).

cases.input: We want to propose that our team adopt vendor X for the internal data platform. I have benchmark numbers, three competitor quotes, and interview notes with two teams currently using vendor X. Help me put together the deck.
cases.notes: Classic proposal/approval deck. Should produce a filled storyline template and stop. Vendor benchmark numbers are facts; adoption impact projections should be labeled Inference or Hypothesis.

grading_rubric.deck_thesis_block_present: output contains all of these headings verbatim: 'Deck thesis', 'Storyline', 'Key objections and risks', 'Open evidence gaps'
grading_rubric.governing_question_is_a_question: the line labeled 'Governing question' ends with '?' and mentions vendor adoption (regex-friendly: matches /adopt|vendor|recommendation/i)
grading_rubric.storyline_table_rows_have_action_titles: the storyline table has >=3 non-empty rows and no 'Action title' cell is a bare topic label (regex reject: /^(overview|introduction|market analysis|background|summary)$/i)
grading_rubric.epistemic_labels_present_per_row: each storyline row's Status column contains one of: Fact, Inference, Hypothesis, Unknown
grading_rubric.handoff_stated: output contains substring 'presentation-architect' OR 'rendering skill' near the end (last 20 lines)
grading_rubric.no_visual_composition_bleed: output MUST NOT contain any of: 'font', 'color', '#RRGGBB', 'slide layout', 'pptx', 'marp', 'chart type:', 'palette', 'typography'

cases.gold_reference_spec:
# Deck thesis
- Audience: platform engineering leads + budget owner
- Current state: uses in-house ETL; aware of vendor X but not evaluated
- Desired outcome: approval to pilot vendor X for 60 days
- Why this matters now: contract renewal window closes in 6 weeks
- Governing question: Should we adopt vendor X for the internal data platform?
- Governing thought: Vendor X meets our benchmark targets at lower TCO than the two competing quotes, and two peer teams report stable production use, so we should run a 60-day pilot.
- Epistemic status of governing thought: Inference (benchmarks are Fact; TCO delta is Inference; peer-team stability is Fact within 6-month window)

# Storyline
| # | Action title | Role | Evidence | Visual idea | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Renewal deadline forces a decision in 6 weeks | opening | contract doc | text | Fact |
| 2 | Vendor X is 30% faster on our workload than incumbent | evidence | bench.csv | bar chart | Fact |
| 3 | Two peer teams report stable production use | evidence | interview notes | quote block | Fact |
| 4 | Adoption risk is migration cost, not runtime cost | objection | cost model | text | Inference |
| 5 | Recommend 60-day pilot with defined exit criteria | recommendation | plan draft | text | Inference |

# Key objections and risks
- Objection 1: Migration cost may exceed savings -> addressed in beat #4
- Objection 2: Vendor lock-in -> addressed by pilot exit criteria in beat #5

# Open evidence gaps
- Gap 1: Security review not yet requested -> blocking before full rollout, caveat for pilot

# Handoff notes
- Hand off to presentation-architect for slide composition; budget owner is time-constrained (5 min live + leave-behind).

cases.input: I need to present my paper's results to my lab next week. 20 min slot. The main finding is that method A beats method B on three benchmarks but fails on a fourth. Draft the deck for me.
cases.notes: Research/technical deck. Skill must handle the fourth-benchmark failure honestly with an epistemic label, not omit or overclaim. Visual composition should not appear.

grading_rubric.negative_result_row_exists: at least one storyline row's Action title mentions the fourth benchmark failure OR limitation (regex: /fail|not\s+beat|underperform|limitation|does\s+not/i)
grading_rubric.negative_result_not_softened: the negative-result row's Action title MUST NOT contain hedging that erases the result (regex reject: /promising|nearly|almost matches|comparable/i unless followed by explicit numeric evidence)
grading_rubric.governing_question_research_shaped: the governing question mentions when/whether/under-what-conditions method A works (regex: /when|whether|under what|which|why/i)
grading_rubric.necessity_test_marker: output contains phrase 'necessity test' OR an 'Appendix candidates' section with items labeled 'removable' / 'if removed, main argument stands' / equivalent
grading_rubric.no_code_bleed: output MUST NOT contain code fences with 'matplotlib', 'plotly', 'seaborn', 'plt.', 'ax.' , 'go.Figure', or 'import '

cases.gold_reference_spec:
# Deck thesis
- Audience: my lab (PI + 6 grad students, mixed subfields)
- Current state: aware method A exists; do not know benchmark results
- Desired outcome: agree on the boundary of when method A is preferable
- Governing question: On which class of benchmarks does method A outperform method B, and why does it fail on the fourth?
- Governing thought: Method A beats B on structured-input benchmarks (1-3) but degrades on benchmark 4 because it relies on an assumption benchmark 4 violates.
- Epistemic status: Fact for benchmarks 1-3; Inference for the causal explanation of benchmark 4

# Storyline
| # | Action title | Role | Evidence | Visual idea | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Method A wins on 3 of 4 benchmarks | evidence | results.csv | comparison | Fact |
| 2 | Benchmark 4 violates the structured-input assumption | limitation | data schema | text | Inference |
| 3 | The failure mode maps to a known class we can name | implication | analysis notes | text | Inference |
| 4 | Next: extend method A to unstructured inputs | next-action | roadmap | text | Hypothesis |

# Open evidence gaps
- Gap 1: We have not tested benchmarks 5-8 in the same family -> caveat, not blocking

# Handoff notes
- Hand off to presentation-architect. Live 20-min slot; visuals should carry the comparison and the failure mode.

cases.input: Weekly status update for the platform migration project. Steering committee, 15 minutes. Things are behind on the database side but ahead on the API side. Help me prep the deck.
cases.notes: Meeting/status deck. Skill should reference meeting-decks.md pattern implicitly and land on decisions/asks, not just a report. No visual composition.

grading_rubric.status_pattern_visible: storyline rows include beats matching all four: what changed, implication, risks, next actions (each may be one row or grouped)
grading_rubric.asks_beat_has_actor: at least one row with role in {ask, next-action, recommendation} names an owner OR a date (regex: /owner|by [A-Z]|by \d|due|decision needed/i)
grading_rubric.governing_question_decision_scoped: governing question mentions what the committee must decide, approve, or unblock (regex: /decide|approve|unblock|reprioritize|escalate/i)
grading_rubric.no_visual_prescription: output MUST NOT prescribe specific chart types or colors (regex reject: /traffic light|red\/amber\/green|gantt|progress bar/i)
grading_rubric.both_sides_named: storyline explicitly names both the database-side slippage and the API-side lead (regex: /database/i AND /api/i, both present)

cases.gold_reference_spec:
# Deck thesis
- Audience: steering committee (7 members, mixed technical depth)
- Current state: last update was 2 weeks ago; DB slippage flagged then
- Desired outcome: committee approves DB scope trim OR resource shift
- Governing question: Should we trim database scope or add DB resources to hold the July cutover?
- Governing thought: API is ahead; DB is 3 weeks behind; holding the July cutover requires either a scope trim of the reporting tables or one more DB engineer for 4 weeks.

# Storyline
| # | Action title | Role | Evidence | Visual idea | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | API is 2 weeks ahead of plan | context | burndown | text | Fact |
| 2 | DB is 3 weeks behind due to schema-review loop | context | change log | text | Fact |
| 3 | July cutover slips 2 weeks unless we act | implication | plan | text | Inference |
| 4 | Two options: trim reporting tables OR add 1 DB eng | recommendation | est.md | text | Inference |
| 5 | Ask: committee picks one option this meeting | next-action | - | text | Fact |

# Key objections and risks
- Objection: Adding an engineer may not accelerate a review-bound task -> acknowledge, prefer scope trim

# Handoff notes
- Hand off to presentation-architect. Live, 15 min, decision-oriented.

cases.input: Exec wants a recommendation: build vs buy for our authentication system. I have partial data on build cost, one vendor demo, and no security review yet. Deck due tomorrow.
cases.notes: Decision deck under uncertainty. Must recommend where evidence supports it and label gaps explicitly. Do not manufacture confidence to sound decisive.

grading_rubric.recommendation_present_with_status: output contains a beat whose Role is 'recommendation' AND its Status column is one of {Fact, Inference, Hypothesis}
grading_rubric.security_review_listed_as_gap: the 'Open evidence gaps' section contains a bullet mentioning security review (regex: /security\s+review/i) with a disposition label (blocking / caveat / follow-up)
grading_rubric.options_enumerated: at least 2 distinct options (build, buy) appear as separate rows or in an 'Options and criteria' block (regex: both /build/i and /buy/i present)
grading_rubric.no_false_certainty: the recommendation Action title MUST NOT be labeled Status=Fact if the deck-thesis Epistemic status is Inference or Hypothesis (consistency check)
grading_rubric.recommendation_not_deferred_without_reas: if the recommendation is 'defer', it must cite the specific missing evidence, not a vague 'need more data'

cases.gold_reference_spec:
# Deck thesis
- Audience: CTO + VP Eng
- Current state: aware of build path; briefed once on vendor V
- Desired outcome: pick build or buy this week
- Governing question: Should we build the authentication system in-house or buy vendor V?
- Governing thought: Buy vendor V, contingent on passing the security review that we launch this week; build cost estimate exceeds buy 3-year TCO by roughly 2x.
- Epistemic status of governing thought: Inference (build cost is partial; security review is Unknown)

# Storyline
| # | Action title | Role | Evidence | Visual idea | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Two viable options: build vs buy vendor V | opening | scope doc | text | Fact |
| 2 | Build cost estimate: ~$1.4M over 3y (partial) | evidence | cost model | text | Inference |
| 3 | Vendor V 3y TCO: ~$650k (demo + list price) | evidence | quote | text | Inference |
| 4 | Recommend buy V, conditional on security review | recommendation | - | text | Inference |
| 5 | Ask: fund security review this week | next-action | - | text | Fact |

# Open evidence gaps
- Gap 1: Security review of vendor V not yet done -> blocking for final commit, not for direction
- Gap 2: Build cost line items for compliance not scoped -> caveat

# Handoff notes
- Hand off to presentation-architect. Exec audience, prefers a one-page summary + backup.

cases.input: Project kickoff for a new customer-analytics initiative. Cross-functional room: eng, product, sales, data science, exec sponsor. Help me build the kickoff deck.
cases.notes: Kickoff deck. Should not force a rigid framework (three pillars, 10-slide template) but shape structure around what this specific audience needs to agree on.

grading_rubric.cross_functional_ack: output names at least 3 of {eng, product, sales, data science, exec sponsor} explicitly in Audience OR in storyline rows
grading_rubric.why_now_what_how_coverage: storyline rows collectively cover all of: why now, what (scope), how (approach), who (owner), when (timeline)
grading_rubric.no_forced_three_pillar: output MUST NOT emit exactly 3 sibling rows labeled 'pillar' or a 3-column framework label (regex reject: /three pillars|3 pillars/i)
grading_rubric.no_brand_visual_bleed: output MUST NOT mention logo, brand, stock photo, hero image, template
grading_rubric.open_scope_gaps_flagged: the 'Open evidence gaps' section is non-empty and at least one gap is about scope or success metric

cases.gold_reference_spec:
# Deck thesis
- Audience: cross-functional room (eng, product, sales, DS, exec sponsor)
- Current state: initiative announced by exec; scope not agreed across functions
- Desired outcome: leave the room with agreed scope, owner list, and phase-1 timeline
- Governing question: What is in scope for phase 1 of the customer-analytics initiative, and who owns what by when?
- Governing thought: Phase 1 delivers the churn-scoring model to sales in 10 weeks; scope excludes real-time inference and pricing analytics.

# Storyline
| # | Action title | Role | Evidence | Visual idea | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Why now: sales asked for churn signal in QBR | context | QBR notes | text | Fact |
| 2 | Phase 1 scope: churn scoring, batch, weekly | scope | draft SOW | text | Inference |
| 3 | Approach: reuse feature store; new model service | how | arch sketch | diagram | Inference |
| 4 | Owners: DS-lead model, Eng-lead pipeline, PM-lead intake | who | RACI | text | Fact |
| 5 | Timeline: 10 weeks, review gates at 3/6/10 | when | plan | text | Inference |
| 6 | Out of scope for phase 1: real-time, pricing | scope | - | text | Fact |

# Open evidence gaps
- Gap 1: Success metric definition not agreed with sales -> blocking for phase-1 signoff
- Gap 2: Data retention policy for scoring outputs -> follow-up

# Handoff notes
- Hand off to presentation-architect. Cross-functional live 45-min working session.

cases.input: Can you make the title slide look cleaner and pick a better chart type for slide 4? Here's the current deck.
cases.notes: Near-miss / boundary case. User is asking for visual polish on an existing deck. This skill must recognize the request is out of scope and hand off. Producing a storyline here would be over-reach.

grading_rubric.explicit_decline: output contains a decline sentence (regex: /out of scope|not this skill|belongs to|hand(ing)? off|use .* instead/i)
grading_rubric.names_correct_handoff_target: output contains the substring 'presentation-architect' (correct handoff for visual composition)
grading_rubric.no_storyline_produced: output MUST NOT contain the heading 'Storyline' with a filled table (>=2 rows). A brief mention that a storyline was NOT generated is fine.
grading_rubric.no_visual_prescription_in_reply: output MUST NOT prescribe a chart type, font, or color (regex reject: /use a (bar|line|pie) chart|font-family|hex code|#[0-9a-f]{3,6}/i)
grading_rubric.reason_stated: output states WHY it declines (not just refusal): mentions storyline vs visual composition distinction

cases.gold_reference_spec:
This request is about visual composition (chart type, title-slide layout), not storyline design. The deck-storyline skill does not handle chart selection, typography, or slide-level layout choices.

Hand off to the `presentation-architect` skill, which owns:
- visual grammar selection (chart type by data relationship)
- slide-level composition (focal point, reading order, emphasis)
- text density and mode calibration

If the underlying argument on slide 4 still needs sharpening (e.g., action title is a topic label, not a takeaway), come back to `deck-storyline` first. Otherwise, `presentation-architect` is the right next step.

cases.input: Team retrospective for the Q2 launch. 10 people attended, mostly engineers plus PM and QA. I want to walk through what went well, what didn't, and what we'll change next quarter.
cases.notes: Boundary case: retrospective archetype not covered explicitly by the current test set. Skill should treat it like a decision deck for the team's next-quarter behavior, not as a report.

grading_rubric.governing_question_is_change_shaped: governing question mentions what the team should change/keep/stop next quarter (regex: /change|keep|stop|start|next\s+quarter|adopt|abandon/i) and ends with '?'
grading_rubric.three_beats_present: storyline rows collectively cover all three of: went well, did not go well, change/commitment (each may be one or more rows)
grading_rubric.action_titles_specific: at least 3 storyline rows have Action titles that name a concrete artifact, process, or metric (regex reject: /communication|collaboration|teamwork|synergy|process improvement/ as the whole title)
grading_rubric.causes_labeled_epistemically: any 'why it happened' row is labeled Inference or Hypothesis, not Fact (unless the row cites direct data)
grading_rubric.no_visual_composition: output MUST NOT prescribe layout, font, color, chart type, or slide count

cases.gold_reference_spec:
# Deck thesis
- Audience: launch team (7 engineers, 1 PM, 1 QA, 1 EM)
- Current state: launch shipped 1 week late; team morale mixed
- Desired outcome: agree on 2-3 concrete process changes for Q3
- Governing question: Which 2-3 changes should we commit to for Q3 to avoid a repeat of the Q2 slip?
- Governing thought: The Q2 slip was driven by late API contract changes; committing to a contract freeze at week 4 and a QA-embed in sprint 2 would prevent the two largest delay classes we observed.
- Epistemic status: Inference on the causal claim (based on 3 slippage tickets), Fact on the ship date and QA finding count

# Storyline
| # | Action title | Role | Evidence | Visual idea | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Q2 shipped 1 week late; scope held | context | plan vs actual | text | Fact |
| 2 | Went well: on-call load stayed flat post-launch | went-well | pager stats | text | Fact |
| 3 | Did not go well: 3 late API contract changes | did-not | ticket log | text | Fact |
| 4 | Likely cause: contracts finalized in-sprint | inference | retro notes | text | Inference |
| 5 | Commit: freeze API contract by week 4 | change | - | text | Inference |
| 6 | Commit: embed QA in sprint 2 planning | change | - | text | Inference |

# Open evidence gaps
- Gap 1: We have 3 slippage cases; sample too small to generalize -> caveat, revisit after Q3

# Handoff notes
- Hand off to presentation-architect. Working session format, low-formality, 45 min.

cases.input: Can you help me write a one-page memo to my manager explaining why we should sunset the legacy reporting service?
cases.notes: Boundary case: user asks for a memo, not a deck. Skill scope excludes single messages / short notes. Should decline and re-anchor on what output form fits the task.

grading_rubric.explicit_decline_as_out_of_scope: output contains a decline sentence naming 'memo' or 'not a deck' (regex: /memo.*not|not (a )?deck|single (message|note)/i)
grading_rubric.no_storyline_table: output MUST NOT include the heading 'Storyline' followed by a filled markdown table
grading_rubric.no_deck_thesis_block: output MUST NOT include the heading '# Deck thesis' with filled fields
grading_rubric.no_presentation_architect_handoff: output MUST NOT recommend 'presentation-architect' as the next step (because no deck is being produced)
grading_rubric.constructive_redirect: output offers a next step (write the memo directly, use a different skill, or asks whether the memo should later become a deck)

cases.gold_reference_spec:
This is a one-page memo, not a deck. The `deck-storyline` skill designs multi-slide arguments and is not the right tool for a single-page written note.

Do NOT hand off to `presentation-architect` either -- that skill also assumes a deck output.

Suggested next step: draft the memo directly in prose. If the memo will later be presented (e.g., you plan to walk the room through it as slides), come back to `deck-storyline` at that point with the memo as source material.

cases.input: I have three months of research findings on internal developer productivity. Help me figure out how to structure MY presentation of the findings.
cases.notes: Boundary case: user frames the deck around themselves. Skill must re-anchor on the audience concern per the SKILL.md rule that governing questions correspond to real audience concerns, not author reporting.

grading_rubric.audience_reanchor_explicit: output contains a sentence that re-anchors on the audience (regex: /audience|who is (this|the deck) for|whose decision|what should they/i) BEFORE any storyline table
grading_rubric.governing_question_is_not_author_shaped: governing question MUST NOT match /how do I (structure|present|organize) my/i and MUST be about an audience decision or belief change
grading_rubric.audience_and_desired_outcome_prompted: output either fills the Audience and Desired outcome lines or explicitly asks the user to specify them before storyline generation continues
grading_rubric.action_titles_are_takeaways: at least 3 storyline rows (if generated) have Action titles that state a takeaway, not a finding category label (reject: 'Findings on X', 'Category Y', 'Section Z')
grading_rubric.handoff_stated_only_if_storyline_complet: if the skill returns a filled storyline, it names 'presentation-architect' as the handoff; if it stops to ask for audience clarification, no handoff needed

cases.gold_reference_spec:
Before we can structure the deck, we need to anchor on the audience, not the findings. 'How do I present my findings' is an author-shaped question; the deck has to answer an audience-shaped question.

Before I fill the storyline template, please confirm:
- Audience: who will see this? (eng leadership? platform team? whole R&D?)
- Current state: what do they believe about developer productivity today?
- Desired outcome: what decision, belief, or action should change?

Once those are named, the governing question typically reshapes into something like:
- 'Which two productivity interventions should we invest in for H2?'
rather than
- 'How do I organize my findings?'

Provisional draft, assuming eng leadership as audience:

# Deck thesis
- Audience: eng leadership (VP + 4 directors)
- Current state: aware productivity is a concern; no shared view of biggest lever
- Desired outcome: pick 2 interventions to fund in H2
- Governing question: Which two interventions from the study should we fund in H2 to move developer productivity most?
- Governing thought: Fund CI-speed reduction and on-call rotation redesign; together they address the two largest observed drags on flow.

# Storyline
| # | Action title | Role | Evidence | Visual idea | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Two drags dominate: CI wait time and on-call load | evidence | study.csv | ranked bar | Fact |
| 2 | CI-speed fix costs less, ships faster | recommendation | est.md | text | Inference |
| 3 | On-call redesign is higher-leverage over 12 months | recommendation | model | text | Inference |

# Handoff notes
- Hand off to presentation-architect once audience is confirmed.
